purpose: Selected historical language material for continuous development and a reading-to-science retention experiment.
policy: Founders begin with random weights and the fixed 256-byte vocabulary. Only the selected source texts below enter foundation training. Validation and test books never supply weight updates or teacher targets. Synthetic numerical tests use separate disposable models.
stage_note: Stages order increasing reading complexity. They are engineering curriculum labels, not measured human ages or evidence of general intelligence.

stages.name: Words and simple sentences
stages.focus: Familiar objects, actions, short sentences and basic questions.

stages.name: Connected reading
stages.focus: Longer sentences, relationships and short stories.

stages.name: Longer stories and explanations
stages.focus: Broader vocabulary, event sequences and longer passages.

stages.name: Descriptive natural science
stages.focus: Longer explanatory passages on light, air, water, plants and insects; historical language training, not modern scientific ground truth.

sources.title: McGuffey's Eclectic Primer, Revised Edition
sources.author: William Holmes McGuffey
sources.reason: Starts with simple vocabulary and gradually introduces short sentences and lessons.

sources.title: McGuffey's First Eclectic Reader, Revised Edition
sources.author: William Holmes McGuffey
sources.reason: Elementary reading about familiar objects, actions and everyday situations.

sources.title: McGuffey's Second Eclectic Reader
sources.author: William Holmes McGuffey
sources.reason: Progresses to connected reading and short stories.

sources.title: McGuffey's Third Eclectic Reader
sources.author: William Holmes McGuffey
sources.reason: Adds longer passages and more varied vocabulary.

sources.title: New National First Reader
sources.author: Charles J. Barnes, Harlan H. Ballard and S. Proctor Thayer
sources.reason: A separate elementary reader for model selection, excluded from learning.

sources.title: The Beacon Second Reader
sources.author: James H. Fassett
sources.reason: A separate collection of reading passages reserved for final evaluation.

sources.title: The Fairy-Land of Science
sources.author: Arabella B. Buckley
sources.reason: An explicit change from elementary reading stories to sustained explanations of physical and natural phenomena. Historical scientific claims require separate modern verification.

sources.title: Home Geography for Primary Grades
sources.author: C. C. Long
sources.reason: A different author and book with descriptive lessons on surroundings, weather, land and water, held out to assess transfer to related explanatory prose; not a fact-answer key.
